subject: RRBS No Controls, just treatment sample.

messages.author: 50cbd3343b477fe0
messages.subject: RRBS No Controls, just treatment sample.
parts: Hi I have RRBS data without any biological controls. I am simply looking for stats and distribution of methylation sites near genes, promoters etc. So i don't want to perform differential methylation analysis. Actually I want to use "meth" object instead of myDiff23 [diffAnn=annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p,gene.obj)]. I hope you understand my question. I have basic knowledge of R. any help in this regard is greatly appreciated. Thank you!

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] RRBS No Controls, just treatment sample.
parts:
Hi,

It is very much possible to achieve your objective with methylKit!

While working with multiple samples, it is obligatory to give a treatment vector that indicates control and test samples. However, the use of this vector is only in calculating differential methylation. So, you may chose any combination of treatment vector for your samples and perform "unite" to get a meth object (methylBase obj)

All the best!

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] RRBS No Controls, just treatment sample.
parts:
annotate.WithGenicParts() and alike can also take GRanges objects as arguments. So you can coerce your methylKit objects (see vignette) and use those functions on GRanges objects.

Best,
Altuna
